newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Germany edge to solve VW subsidy row.
newsitem.headline: EU, Germany edge to solve VW subsidy row.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG plans an investment in Kassel, in the state of Essen, to solve a conflict with the European Commission over illegal subsidies, a Commission spokesman said on Friday.
He did not give any details but said that the German government had informed the Commission about the plan in March and that more data were expected.
The move follows a dispute last year over aid granted by the German state of Saxony to help finance VW investment projects despite an adverse Commission ruling.
It was the first time Germany had openly challenged the EU's authority to control national subsidies to businesses.

The Commission cleared in June 1996 almost 540 million marks in German regional subsidies to VW's Mosel and Chemnitz plants, in Saxony. This was 241 million marks less than the amount Volkswagen had been promised by Saxony.

The powerful carmaker has said publicly that it could invest elsewhere in Germany to compensate for the illegal money already paid. Van Miert has said he would examine such a plan as a possible remedy.
In a move to defuse a crisis with the Commission, the German central government undertook last year to neutralise the illegal aid by blocking a similar amount in tax rebates.

The Commission has become increasingly worried that public subsidies may have gone out of control in Germany, despite accepting that industrial restructuring in the states previously under communist rule is a costly and lengthy process.
